searchText: Participation rate is still at 75% on pyrmont? I wanted to check with my own node waiting for 6 seconds on block 0 https://pyrmont.beaconcha.in/epochs has it at 77 atm, it dropped for a while earlier in the week but seems back to a happy state 77 is not so happy state if 90% of the active validators are held by dev teams + EF true, not perfect - but at least finalizing. most of the teku team are away, so i'm kind of glad our validators are happy! looking at the chart now it does not seem to have been recovered from a couple of weeks ago I think I'll set up a beacon in a different laptop then to run pyrmont cause the same server that I use for mainnet won't take the current status probably i ended up downloading and starting from an SSZ state snapshot I only stopped my beacon a couple of days ago so I can just resync from there, shouldn't take long yep that'll be fine i would have been from 0, not a fun time I'll wait a couple of days to see if it gets to a more stable situation, if it does I'll just restart it on my same computer, since what I'm interested to check is against the same environment wether waiting 6 secs helps or not. I may directly test on mainnet, is such a simple patch that I doubt I'll be slashed for it 🙂 wait for 6 seconds, just to make sure block has been produced? But regarding this patch: can you tell me if Teku (or any other client for that matter) waits 4 seconds but stops waiting if it receives the block before? It seems prysm waits 4 seconds no matter what (but I may be reading the code wrong) teku will wait until 1/3 through the epoch to see if a block is produced, then assume the block didnt get produced if its not seen the spec says to act eagerly if receiving a valid block from the expected proposer before the 4s time yes wait 6 seconds on slot 0 on mainnet would have saved me all the lost wait on target vote in the last couple of weeks if teku gets a block at teh very start of epoch, it wont wait slot i mean *sigh* Thanks, this is why I suspect I am reading the code wrongfully in prysm but I coudln't find where the wait is cancelled it improves chances of getting attestation included if you can skip out of the wait it could certainly be overlooked If the wait is indeed cancelled then I'll just apply my patch on mainnet and test there cause then the impact should really be minimal as long as you only skip once you get that block it should just have an improved chance of inclusion of the attestation, at least thats the theory i think we're running on This operates under the assumption that your attestation will be well propagated and picked up in an aggregate (or otherwise end up in a node's pool that has a chance to produce a block in the next 31 slots) Well, the question here is to measure the impact of loosing on inclusion distance (or possibly not getting included at all) vs loosing target+head vote oh, I'm suggesting you might lose inclusion entirely depending on the mechanics yep... Adrian could answer definitively, this is just my understanding of what teku does (i've still got a lot to learn) because at 8s aggregates are produced I checked all my wrong target+head votes on mainnet in the last two weeks were because of slots that just arrived less than a second after the 4 seconds mark if you don't make it into an aggregate, then you are hoping that you get picked up in someones pool as a single sometime in the next 31 slots yeh so when you wait your chance of getting included at slot+1 goes way down because it has to get to an aggregator I understand being late isn't that bad, but you risk not getting included at all but depending on attestation propagation rates, risk might not be taht bad I don't have good visibility on it right now yeh I'm definitely not an expert on the topic I do agree that tuning the time *might* lead to better results in current network conditions! the "timeliness" incentive is also a bit off (meaning it doesn't incentivize timeliness that well) and is expected to be tuned in first hardfork (see vitalik's accounting reform PR if interested) making sure you have a good mix of peers from subnets is the other big thing i guess yeah, I'm not sure how this will fare, but I want to test it and somehow pyrmont is not a choice for me now. Also since this is slot 0 only the impact will be minimal for me but if the wait is always there in prysm instead of only when the block does not arrive, then it will be a problem yeah, understood. excited to see the results right cause then I'll be submitting all slot zero attestations after 6 seconds which isn't great yeah that I don't want to do, I asked the guys at prysm, will see if they confirm my fear if prysm doesn't due opportunistic attestation broadcasts, this is a great place for an optimization I haven't been keeping my eye on pyrmont. does look sickly the problem is that pyrmont by itself is resource hungry, and with the increase in active validators on mainnet resources have increased substantially there too, so I started missing head votes in mid-epoch. I killed the pyrmont node and went back to attesting fine, so I am reluctant of resyncing until it's in a more stable situation curious, what's your bottleneck at home? bandwidth, cpu, or memory? looking at https://pyrmont.eth2.wtf/#/ we have a long way to go on memory optimization the way attestations are currently structured is a linear increase in bandwidth and cpu load I think there is a way to get the overall bandwidth down for home nodes without too much trouble, but the peak load would still be similar in the worst case I'm pretty concerned about growing load. plan on spending some time in early january to flesh out some proposals both RAM and bandwidth are pretty bad here, at 16Gb Ram, geth mainnet takes at least 6 (other than just continued client optimizations) and each beacon node is taking more than 2 on mainnet and 3 for pyrmont minimal, when pyrmont didn't finalize that explodes right that's majorly due to lack of pruning in the fork choice. which there are some straightforward ways to optimize but not sure if any client is yet. Nimbus was talking about it Nimbus on pyrmont is 1.3GB memoryat stable network. Definitely want to get clients in the 1 to 4 range. Prysm did improve a lot after the latest medalla incident in memory consumption 3GB on on pyrmont for which node type? looks like some clients are *much* more than that but not that low as 1.3Gb 3GB the beaconchain on my box currently 2.3 in mainnet prysm? but the 3Gb figure was prysm before finality hit let me give you the figure a couple of days ago will have to tunnel grafana (I'm on a cell) no rush about to go pick up some sushi it averaged at 2.6Gb and I killed it at 3Gb after the non-finality on pyrmont yes prysm <@755590043632140352> the bottleneck for us is slashing protection Thats the reason participation is so low on our end Weve known this is the case for a while but will not able to resolve until we are back Hence the poor testnet performance in our nodes over the holidays <@!311971895828283393> can you confirm the issue of the wait of 4 seconds please? I am about to propose where to change that if that's the case, in #design-review on your channel Apologies not available to do so, will make note of it for next week saw a slashing, didn't realise it was pyrmont initially but kinda glad it was! I think proto even managed to slash a couple of his Teku nodes 🙂 eep The slashings I can see on pyrmont.beaconcha.in are all from post-genesis validators (ie not the ones run by dev teams or EF) They were included in blocks by some of the genesis validators but can't see any instances of genesis validators being slashed yet. ok well that was a lot quicker for you to check than me! I was thinking that was my afternoon gone! What makes you say that? I can see 3 slashings in the last day on Pyrmont and none involve EF Teku nodes at all. Oh I see the couple of EF Teku nodes slashed back in November. Not sure what the timing of Proto rearranging all the EF validators, but I'm guessing it was then and something wound up running same keys in multiple places. Yep, those two At the time validators were assigned differently, it may not be teku. Will try and check which client I was running them on. But yes, looks like two validators didn't go through restarts and switches safely. We need standardized protection Ohh I see It's in the last 100 validators of our batch We gave those away for experimental usage And they did get slashed When we reorganized the validators the labeling must have missed that edge case 19900-19999 is not us <@340345049063882753> <@755590043632140352> Will get those labeled correctly again That’s excellent news. I may need another week at the beach to get over the heart attack I got from Paul messaging saying we were being slashed mind you... They were correctly labeled as "experimental" before. Contacted beaconchain explorer to help fix it. When we reorganized all validators and updated labeling it was missed. Hence it not showing up before, even though the slashings happened a long time ago sorry about that 😦 i mighta freaked out a little, i appreciated the help a lot! Indeed a bug from our end, thanks <@!755590043632140352> for reporting this. We had the correct behavior back in April during Topaz testnet but it got altered after I posted in bug-report a picture of my vim session working on the same approach to fix it 😦 Next time I won't report until I have the PR ready, perhaps that way I'll beat you I'll merge that branch and patch it to wait 6 seconds on slot 0 and try it on pyrmont Looking good <@!363800010518822915> since I applied your patch all blocks that are actually received are now being attested at 0.8s instead of 4s, that has to have a real impact! I am on a very stressed node so in real life behaviour will be better. Will continue monitoring in pyrmont until I get a couple of slot 0 to attest and check the wait of 6 seconds approach (it's already patched here to wait 6 seconds on slot 0) I am however reluctant to apply this on mainnet cause it's a little scary the area of the code your patch touches 😄 so I'll wait for your soak testing Please dont apply this on the mainnet yet. Let's get enough soak time on pyrmont first. We'll roll this out to our pyrmont clusters next week. With 20% of the network, it should give us much better data point Happy new year everyone! Happy new year guys!
